# Analyze Season 2 yellowtail patterns by day and class
df = tables['trips']
s2 = df[df['fished_date_season'] == 2].copy()

# Group by fished_date_doy and cls to see patterns
doy_patterns = s2.groupby(['fished_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'landing': 'count'
}).reset_index()

doy_patterns['yt_per_angler'] = doy_patterns['yt'] / doy_patterns['anglers']
doy_patterns['yt_per_trip'] = doy_patterns['yt'] / doy_patterns['landing']

# Focus on DOY 260-310 range
key_range = doy_patterns[(doy_patterns['fished_date_doy'] >= 260) & (doy_patterns['fished_date_doy'] <= 310)]
print("Season 2 Yellowtail by DOY and Class (DOY 260-310):")
print(key_range.sort_values('fished_date_doy').to_string())

# Find the biggest days
top_days = s2.groupby('fished_date_doy').agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'landing': 'count'
}).reset_index()
top_days['yt_per_angler'] = top_days['yt'] / top_days['anglers']
top_days['yt_per_trip'] = top_days['yt'] / top_days['landing']
top_days = top_days.sort_values('yt_per_trip', ascending=False)

print("\n\nTop 20 DOY by yt/trip in Season 2:")
print(top_days.head(20)[['fished_date_doy', 'yt', 'anglers', 'landing', 'yt_per_trip', 'yt_per_angler']].to_string())
